summary.text:
Chichester carries no external debt. Paragraph 4.21 states 'the Council is debt-free and is an investor' and Table 6 sets CFR and external borrowing at zero for every year to 2029-30; our PWLB price book returns no borrower on any variant of the name. This is a treasury management annual outturn scoped to investments only.

The book is £118.757m at 31 March 2026 (up £7.237m from £111.520m), and the story is on the lender side. £51m sits as Local Authority Investments (Table 1) — up £14m in the year and 62% of the £81.995m internally managed book, the biggest LA-lending position we have seen among the districts we have read. On the Arlingclose sheet at p.9 Chichester's £81.8m internal book is roughly three times the 40-English-Non-Met-District average of £27.5m.

The duration shape is distinctive. 227 days weighted-average maturity against a 45-day similar-LA benchmark, and £55m out beyond 364 days against an £80m limit. The book earned 4.42% internal against 4.14% sector, and 4.96% total against 4.67% — a deliberately long book that paid off in a falling-rate year. Same shape as Basingstoke and Deane (263 vs 52 days) on a larger investment base. Bail-in exposure fell from 29% to 13%, against a 58% peer average.

Table 3 bakes in £3.921m of treasury income for 2026-27 — £2.1m below the 2025-26 outturn of £6.030m. Alongside that, para 4.9 quotes Arlingclose's central case that Bank Rate will be held at 3.75% 'for the foreseeable future', which today's forward market disagrees with.

officer.body:
Hi Jifang,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the Treasury Management outturn report that went to Corporate Governance and Audit Committee on 13 July. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it.

A cross-check first, which comes out unusually clean. Our PWLB price book returns no borrower on any variant of Chichester. That ties with paragraph 4.21 ("the Council is debt-free and is an investor") and paragraph 4.22 ("the Council is debt free it currently holds no fixed long-term borrowing"), and with the zeros running through the CFR and external-borrowing rows of Table 6 out to 2029-30. There is nothing to reconcile because there is nothing there — one of a small handful of councils in our library that carry no PWLB and no other external debt either. Worth naming in case the fact is ever useful.

Where we might be genuinely useful is on the other side of the book. Your £51m of Local Authority Investments in Table 1, up £14m in the year, is the biggest LA-lending position we've seen among the districts we've read — 62% of the £82m internally managed book, and on the Arlingclose sheet at page 9 your £81.8m internal total is roughly three times the 40-English-Non-Met-District average. That puts Chichester firmly on the lender side of the intra-LA market, and that market is the one nobody publishes distribution for — every council sees its own trades and none sees where they sit against the sector. We track it across the library, so what other authorities are actually paying and offering for one-month, three-month, six-month and one-year money is visible rather than inferred. For context on the borrowing side, July's PWLB drawings were £368m across 33 loans from just 19 borrowers at an average 5.02% — a thin month, which shapes what deposit rates you're likely to be offered next. That breakdown is at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity.

The other distinctive figure is duration. Appendix B gives you 227 days weighted-average maturity against 45 days for similar LAs, with £55m out beyond 364 days against an £80m limit. That is a deliberately long book, and this year it paid off — 4.42% internal against 4.14% sector, and 4.96% total against 4.67%. Where forward yields sit for that maturity range is on the live dashboard at pwlbtoday.org/dashboard — the same dashboard also runs the CIPFA liability benchmark interactively, which for a debt-free council is trivially satisfied today but a useful frame for how much investment cushion is genuinely needed as reserves are drawn down over the medium term.

One data point from your paper that reads as a testable assumption. Paragraph 4.9 quotes Arlingclose's central case that Bank Rate will be held at 3.75% "for the foreseeable future". Today's SONIA/OIS curve prices one-year rates closer to 4.1% — the market is nearer a rise than a hold. Not a call one way or the other, but a difference the Members' workshop on 16 November might want to test against the 2026-27 income budget of £3.92m (Table 3), which sits £2.1m below this year's £6.03m outturn.

On training, four fit. Intra-LA borrowing & lending markets is the most directly relevant given the shape of your book. Investment strategy for debt-free councils speaks to the wider position. Liability Benchmark: the essentials is worth watching given where CIPFA is heading with the Prudential and Treasury Codes. And Members' introduction to treasury is written for exactly the November workshop. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/
